[[Deep North]] |Snow-capped hills and forests with frozen rivers, inhabited by [[Moose]], [[Elaking]], and [[Gammeltroll|Gammeltrolls]]. |Northern edge of the world |} == Alternative biomes == Each biome patch has a chance to have modifiers applied to it on world generation, but only a certain distance from the world center. These modifiers can have the following effects: * Affect foliage, like more [[Raspberries]] or only [[Birch]]es in the Meadows, or only stubs in the Black Forest * Generate additional structures, like [[Large Bone]]s in the Swamps, Plains or Mistlands, or more [[Tar Pit]]s in the Plains * Increase the chance for [[creature level|starred]] creatures * Enable the spawning of certain creatures not normally encountered in the biome, such as [[Bat]]s in the Swamp, or increase existing chances for a creature to spawn, like more [[Abomination]]s * Disable the spawning of creatures native to the biome Several modifiers can affect a single area at once. The following biomes can be affected: * [[Meadows#Alternative biomes|Meadows]] has 8 modifiers. * [[Black Forest#Alternative biomes|Black Forests]] have 8 modifiers. * [[Swamp#Alternative biomes|Swamps]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mountain#Alternative biomes|Mountains]] have 3 modifiers. * [[Plains#Alternative biomes|Plains]] have 5 modifiers. * [[Mistlands#Alternative biomes|Mistlands]] have 6 modifiers. Oceans, the Ashlands and the Deep North do not have any alternative variants. ==Trivia== *The term "biome" comes from the [[wikipedia:biome|ecological concept of the same name]]. *At ''Valheim's'' early access launch in February 2021, five of the planned nine biomes were made available to explore. The other four were accessible, but lacked any meaningful content. ** As of the full release in September 2026, all biomes excluding the Ocean are fully implemented. An Ocean overhaul was ultimately abandoned, with the argument that it only serves the role of a highway between other biomes, which do have meaningful content. * Alternative biomes were introduced in the [[1.0]] release. {{Biomes}} [[de:Biom]] [[ru:Биомы]] [[pt-br:Biomas]] [[uk:Біоми]] [[cs:Biomy]] [[zh-tw:生物群落]] [[Category:Biomes| ]]

[[File:Greyling 0S.png|thumb|A [[greyling]], an aggressive creature found in the [[Meadows]].]] '''Creatures''' are non-player characters which are found throughout ''[[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]''. They can be split to four categories: * [[Creatures#Bosses|Bosses]] are powerful aggressive creatures that must be summoned. Killing them unlocks [[Forsaken power|Forsaken powers]], increases [[Global Keys|world difficulty]] and provides loot to progress in the game. * [[Creatures#Minibosses|Minibosses]] are unique, named, aggressive creatures that you can find in specific dungeons. Killing any given miniboss will reward with one of [[Hildir's Chests]]. * [[Creatures#Aggressive creatures|Aggressive creatures]] will attack players when alerted. They also drop loot when killed. * [[Creatures#Passive creatures|Passive creatures]] provide resources when killed (or harvested). They will never attack players. * [[Creatures#NPCs|NPCs]] are friendly creatures/characters that cannot be killed and may provide some service or help to the player. == Bosses == Bosses, also known as the '''Forsaken''', can be summoned by offering specific items (hinted by the [[Runestone#Altar Runestones|Runestones]]) at their specific spawn site. They have increased HP and special attacks compared to regular creatures. A boss site is automatically marked on the player's map by reading the runestone in the specific biomes. There are multiple spawn locations for every boss. One-star creatures have double the health and deal 150% damage, while two-stars have triple the health and deal double damage. '''Behavior''' *Creatures will give up chasing after unable to attack for 60 seconds or unable to detect the target for 30 seconds. *Some creatures have a max chase range. After chasing that far they will give up if unable to detect the target for 1 seconds. *After unable to attack for 15 seconds, creatures will focus structures for 15 seconds if they can't reach the target. *Creatures only attack walls and doors if they aren't able to reach the target player. *Some creatures are afraid of fire and will flee from it. *Some creatures try to avoid fire and will be passive near it. *Some creatures circulate around the target while waiting to attack. *Swimming creatures try to flee towards water if forced on ground. *Creatures passively regenerate 1.67% of their max health every minute (100% over 60 minutes). *Creatures gain +30% more effective health per each additional player within 100 meters. E.g. 3 players = +60% effective health. **This is updated whenever the creature takes damage. *Creatures gain +4% more damage per each additional player within 100 meters. '''Copper Ore''' can be refined into [[Copper]] in a [[Smelter]].

Two Copper can be further processed at a [[Forge]] with [[Tin]] to yield [[Bronze]].

== Availability ==
It can be mined from [[Copper Deposit]]s which can be found in [[Black Forest]] [[biomes]] using any [[Pickaxes (skill)|Pickaxe]]. Such deposits have subtle bronze-colored streaks that reflect the sunlight. It is the only visual feature that distinguishes them from typical stone boulders.

Copper deposits are generated in a large size which extends down into the ground, so digging deep underneath the surface is necessary to fully extract a single deposit.

== Notes ==
* A way of farming Copper is to dig the earth all around the deposit until it crumbles on itself into Copper Ores. 
* Like other metals, Copper Ore cannot be teleported without a [[Portal stone]].
* The attacks of a [[Troll]], despite being harmless to normal terrain, cause immense damage to Copper Ore. If the player has no pickaxe or simply yearns for a change from their usual monotonous mining method, a Troll can make for a great alternative.

From knarrs to imposing warships, build legendary vessels to conquer the seas and discover new lands.https://www.valheimgame.com/home/#anchor2}} Valheim features an extensive '''building''' system that can be utilized to design structures to meet the demands of any discriminating warrior. In addition to humble homes and outposts, players also use this building interface to make enormous bases, elaborate works of art, defenses against the [[Creatures]] of Valheim, and unique tools to aid in their survival. Starting out with simple wooden building components, players will eventually gain access to the ability to create stronger structures with various materials, including stone and metal. == Basics == You can build using a [[Hammer]] within the working area of a [[Workbench]]. * Press [1-8] to select the hammer in the hotbar slot * Press [RMB] to open the build menu * Press [Q/E] to switch [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] category * Press [LMB] to chose [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]], and place it * Press [Middle Mouse Button] to remove [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Scroll the mouse to rotate the [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] * Hold [Shift] to temporarily disable snapping * Hold [Shift] then [Middle Mouse Button] to select [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you are looking at. There are various crafting stations required to be nearby to place certain [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. These include the following: * The [[Workbench]], required to place most [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]] you have unlocked from the beginning or early on, and some late [[:Category:Building structures|Building Blocks]]. The Workbench is immediately available and costs 10 ordinary wood to build. * The [[Forge]], required to place most building parts containing metals. The Forge requires [[copper]] to build, and becomes available once the player can mine and refine [[Copper Ore]]. * The [[Stonecutter]], required to place building parts created out of stone, such as the stone walls some abandoned buildings are made out of. The Stonecutter requires [[iron]] to build, and becomes available once the player can collect and refine [[Scrap Iron]]. * The [[Artisan Table]], required to build some crafting stations that as of Patch 0.142.6 are at the end of implemented progression. The Artisan Table requires [[Dragon Tear|Dragon Tears]] to build, which must be obtained by defeating the fourth boss, [[Moder]] the dragon. == Snap building == Most building components can snap to each other. This allows for quick and easy building, but can be temporarily disabled by holding the appropriate key or button. By default, this is L-Shift on mouse and keyboard, and LT+LB on controller. == Structural integrity == {{Main|Building stability}} If there is not enough support, the building pieces will fall down. You may reinforce the building with walls, beams, and poles. When you move the cursor to the building piece, it shows a color range from blue, to green, to red. Blue indicates that the part is as stable as it can be, as dictated by its material. The closer to red on the spectrum, the less stable the part. Attempting to place additional pieces onto one that is fully red may result in the new part breaking off and dropping the resources used to construct it unless the new part has lower stability requirements. The stability of an individual building piece is determined by its material, the stability of the piece it's anchored to and its position relative to it, each additional piece inheriting a fraction of the previous piece's stability. A directly vertical pole of [[Wood]] or [[Stone]] can rise 16 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Wood Wall]], [[Wood Wall Half]], [[Stone Wall 1x1]], [[Stone Wall 2x1]], [[Stone Wall 4x2]], [[Wood Pole 1 m]], [[Wood Pole 2 m]], [[Stone Pillar]]. A directly vertical pole of [[Corewood]] Logs can rise 24 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. This is true for [[Log Pole 4 m]] and [[Log Pole 2 m]]. A directly vertical [[Wood Iron Pole]] can rise up to 50 meters off the ground before it cannot support another piece of the same material above it. Trees, including those planted by the player, will effectively function as "the ground" for support purposes, allowing for extremely high construction. [[File:Structure integrity.png|thumb|Found on [https://www.reddit.com/r/valheim/comments/lqsxki/updated_psa_structural_support_details/ Reddit /Valheim], thanks to [https://www.reddit.com/user/ToddGeorgeKelly/ user/ToddGeorgeKelly/]]] In order to keep tall structures stable, the tallest point should be reinforced by supports that create the shortest and most vertical path possible down to the ground. It is worth considering raising the terrain as much as possible below a structure, such that the floor and walls are 100% stable (highlighted in blue when moused over). Boulders are also considered terrain when calculating stability, so parts that intersect them are considered grounded. == Decay == If wooden building sections are not covered during rain, are not linked to a roof, or are submerged in water, they will decay to a maximum of 50% durability and will seem rotting until fixed. When exposed to rain, defensive structures do not rot decay. Stone, black marble, and crystal structures will not decay when wet or submerged. Building the desired structure's roof first, with the appropriate supports and foundation in place, will aid with constructions lasting days or weeks if rain is a worry. == Damage == Player, monster, and creature attacks can all damage structures. Defensive structures will also receive minor damage while causing harm to creatures that come into contact with them. Aggressive creatures are drawn to and hostile toward all light sources (excluding Jack-o-turnips) and crafting stations, and will try to break them if not attacking a player. == Repair == You can repair building parts that seem to be decaying or damaged with a [[Hammer]]. This does not cost any resources, but does consume stamina. The player must be in range of a crafting station that corresponds to the part being repaired, e.g. a [[Workbench]] when repairing a wooden part, or a [[Stonecutter]] for a stone part. == Abandoned buildings == These structures are a type of [[point of interest]] that can be found to naturally occur in the world. The size, layout, and materials these structures are made of can vary greatly as each is generated from random templates. There are different types of abandoned structures such as Abandoned Cabins, Abandoned Towers, Abandoned Farms just to name a few. These abandoned and generated structures can contain things such as chests with items specific to the biome, monsters (usually [[Skeleton]]s), [[:Category:Creature spawner|monster spawner]]s, and [[wikipedia:Vegvísir|Vegvisir]]s to mark the nearest boss altar for that biome. In the Meadows/Black Forest biome, they can also contain naturally spawning [[Beehive]]s, which will drop a [[Queen Bee]] and sometimes [[Honey]] when destroyed. Players should approach abandoned villages with caution since some villages have been reoccupied by [[Draugr]] and [[Draugr Elite]] who will attack the player on sight. These [[Draugr village|Draugr Villages]] can be identified by partial walls of sharp logs and the buzzing of the [[Creature spawner|spawners]] inside several of the buildings as well as a general miasma and the presence of Draugr both inside and outside the structures. They almost always have a large Mead Hall building that cannot be found anywhere else. There may also be a sentry in a tower armed with a bow who will snipe anything that comes near. == Player base and blocking spawning == {{Main|Player base}} Building certain structures considered to be 'player base' will have the following effects in a radius around them: * Prevent [[creatures|creature]] spawning * Prevent items dropped on the ground from despawning after 1 hour (unless submerged) * Enable player base [[events]] to occur For a full list of player base structures, see [[player base]]. == Base building strategies == [[File:Mordheim server - Guild Castle.jpg|thumb|850x850px]] * Building your outposts in close proximity to '''several biome borders''' grants access to varied resources and allows you to observe the territorial in-fighting of different creatures (complete with loot strewn across the terrain), but can also be dangerous. * Many types of '''defenses''' are possible, both in the form of built objects and altered terrain: ** Creatures cannot dig through terrain, making '''"terrain walls" effectively impenetrable''' to them. Thus the perfect defense is built either with a hoe and a pile of rocks, any pickaxe or ideally a combination of the two. Be warned that terrain alterations may cause stutter just as placing objects does (press F2 to check the number of "instances" loaded). ** A hoe can be used to raise terrain while you're standing on it, allowing you to quickly erect a '''pillar''' to stand on and shoot melee enemies below. Beware that you need a workbench nearby to do this. With practice this is possible during combat. ** Most creatures never jump down from ledges (Fenring and Blobs are exceptions). A '''deep pit''' (around 3 "blocks") is also largely safe, and you can shoot enemies coming close to the ledge. Flying creatures may attack from above if you don't build a roof, however. ** Gates can be destroyed, but '''gaps''' the player jumps over when entering or exiting the base cannot. This trick can be inconvenient, however. Also note that you can '''scale steep terrain''' walls by sprinting and jump-spamming, especially when moving towards a crease (corner) for better traction, while most creatures cannot. ** The most '''FPS-efficient method of defense''' is to build on a few terrain pillars. This minimizes terrain alteration "instances" yet allows you to ignore enemies running around outside, especially if the base entrance requires a quick hop to get on. Note that returning terrain to its roughly native height doesn't remove the FPS hit (unless a true "undo terrain changes" tool is added to the game). ** Workbenches (and campfires) '''disallow enemy spawns''' in their radius, making them surprisingly useful defensive tools. You can hide these in the outer perimeter of your walls or in small pits covered with a few floor tiles to make an area safer. Workbenches also stop dropped items from de-spawning over time, however. ** Doors and gates can be used to create a '''toggle-able bridge''' for carts. Another option to defend your bridge is to hang a gate from a support above it and attach the floor piece to the gate with small gaps on the sides, causing the floor to disappear if the gate is destroyed. ** You can place '''gates in the water''' to block enemies, who will be unable to attack the gates, yet allow boats to pass when opened. * The '''"Level Ground"''' option for the hoe uses the terrain height directly underneath you as the target altitude, though if you hold Shift while clicking it'll use the altitude of the terrain you're pointing at instead. Using this knowledge well may save you a lot of stone and work while landscaping as it only expends stamina and hoe durability. * You can also build a '''"gangplank"''' for enemies to walk on, above your pit base, and put a campfire on it so they'll kill themselves, then catch the loot when it drops down. * Combining a moat with a plateau-based outpost is an interesting option. A [[Bronze Axe]] or better is required to damage it. Birch trees produce [[Wood]] and [[Finewood]] when destroyed. The yield of each type of wood is random, however, a birch tree will always drop 20 pieces of wood total (plus 2 Wood from its stump). It is possible to damage Birch trees by intentionally hitting them with falling [[Beech]] trees. If enough damage is done by falling trees, the Birch tree will be brought down. The trunk can then be rolled downslope (ideally) and repeatedly smashed into obstacles until it shatters into usable lumber. Birch trees can also be destroyed by a [[Troll]]. These methods allow players to acquire [[Finewood]] before being able to craft a [[Bronze Axe]]. Birch trees come in 4 variations: two different shapes, each of which has two biome-dependent variations (which differ in color but not in shape). Each of these shapes can come in two colors: with green leaves (in non-Plains [[Biomes]]) or with yellow leaves (in Plains only). Each Birch tree's color is dependent entirely on which biome it spawns in, but its shape is determined entirely randomly. This attack can be used every 5 seconds when within 2 meters of a player. == Taming == ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming]].'' To tame a wild Boar, players should approach while sneaking to avoid alarming it. If a Boar feels threatened, it will become aggressive, chasing the player until they are out of sight, at which point it will revert to a 'hungry' state. Wild Boars have a predictable combat pattern, charging and then retreating, which can be used to the player's advantage when herding them into a pen ''(recommended to tame)''. Constructing a secure pen is essential to prevent the Boar from escaping and to avoid disruption of the taming process by outside sources. To successfully tame a Boar, players need to feed it {{item link|Raspberries}}, {{item link|Blueberries}}, {{item link|Carrot}}s, {{item link|Onion}}s, {{item link|Turnip}}s, or red {{item link|Mushroom}}s. They will ignore all other foods dropped on the ground. Just drop the food on the ground within one meter, and the Boar will eat, as long as it is not frightened ''(indicated by a red exclamation mark)''. Players can place the food on the ground in a stack, as the Boar will only eat one food from the stack at a time. The taming speed is 30 minutes of real-life gameplay with three pieces of food, '''uninterrupted'''; as long as the Boar does not get frightened and the correct amount of food is on the ground, it should only take 30 minutes. A player must remain in the area for taming to progress. If the Boar becomes frightened at any time during taming, the process will take longer and may require more food. == Tamed == When tamed, Boars seek freedom. If a tamed Boar sees an opening in their fenced area, they will run towards it, which can be used to corral them from place to place. Tamed Boars can be renamed by pressing LShift + E. Interacting with them using E will display the message "(Creature name) loves you" on-screen along with a cloud of pink hearts. They are no longer afraid of fire and require feeding for passive health regeneration. Additionally, tamed Boars lose their anchor to their spawn point, allowing them to move more freely. '''Note:''' ''Boars from abandoned farms and Runestones will retain their anchor point and will always try to return home, making them more challenging to handle. It is recommended to either breed these boars on the spot and move the offspring instead, or to name the original tamed animal and then, once bred, kill it. One issue with using the original animal is that it tends to sit in a corner of a pen, staring at its spawn point, which can interfere with breeding as it does not roam the pen.'' == Breeding == Tamed Boars can breed, provided the Boar is happy and well-fed with berries, carrots, onions, turnips or red mushrooms, along with there being another Boar at least within three meters, and no more than five Boars within at least 10 meters. Once the conditions are met, the Boar will accumulate love points (3) with one another until the pregnancy starts. Successful love point is indicated by pink hearts. After gaining enough love points, the Boar becomes pregnant, which is not visualized. After one minute, the Boar gives birth to a baby Boar ''(piglet)'', visualized by a red cloud. Any Boar can become pregnant, which means that if two Boars breed and one becomes pregnant, they still have the ability to breed and get the other pregnant. Once born, the '''piglet''' will take 50 minutes to mature into an adult. Offspring inherit [[Creature Level|stars]] from the parent that gives birth to it. Offspring are tamed at birth and require a [[Butcher Knife]] or friendly fire to kill. Crops will display a status next to their name when planted until they are fully grown. The ''"Healthy"'' status means the plant is growing. All food crops need cultivated soil. Crops will not grow if any of the three conditions are met: * Wrong biome * Not enough space * Not enough sunlight Some crops can only be planted in certain biome requirements. Planting a crop in the wrong environment will display the ''"Can't grow in this environment"'' status. Most crops require a 1x1 area of free space around them. Other crops, structures, or objects placed within this space will prevent the plant from growing. This is true even for rocks that have been covered by the terrain. Any objects within this free space will cause the "''Needs more room to grow"'' status. Crops require unobstructed view of the sky. Any structures built over a crop will cause the ''"Needs an open sky"'' status, regardless of how high the structure is above the crop. Unique among crops - Vineberry vines need to be 1 away from a flat built wall to climb. It can cross over Window or door openings, but any overhang or break in the wall will stop its growth. Fences and decorative panels count as walls for purpose of trellising. Vineberries needs a greater spacing between plants. Trees are also planted with a Cultivator. Notable resources are: * Small patches of 12 planted [[Barley]] ready to harvest for two barley each. * Small patches of 11 planted [[Flax]] ready to harvest for two flax each. * Next to each [[Bonfire]] there is a 50% chance for a [[Fuling Totem]] on an altar. * [[Loot chest#Plains Chest|Plains Chest]] can be found in various places. * [[Tanning Rack]] can be destroyed for 6 [[Leather Scraps]], 5 [[Flint]] and a [[Deer Hide]]. * Huts can be destroyed for various quantities of Deer hide, [[Bone Fragments]] and [[Wood]]. == Strategy == When raiding a Fuling village, it is highly recommended to use a bow to dispatch the Fulings from afar. Thinning their numbers with ranged attacks before attempting melee combat is exceedingly effective. A fully upgraded [[Draugr Fang]] armed with [[Poison Arrow]]s or [[Needle Arrow]]s is capable of killing a normal, unaware Fuling in a single shot. Aggroing too many Fulings at once may result in the player being overwhelmed. Picking off Fulings with arrows will cut down on the number of enemies to fight, and it will often aggro small groups, which will be far easier to fight than the whole village. Target the sentries in towers and Fuling shamans first: shooting sentries will draw away other Fulings near the tower, and shamans will shield themselves and other Fulings nearby with magic if they are alerted. Running away is always a valid strategy if the player has enough energy to do so. == Notes == * Fuling villages will often be populated by a substantial number of [[Fuling]]s, [[Fuling Shaman]]s, and [[Fuling Berserker]]s. It is not advised that ill-equipped players enter the village; [[Iron]] armor and weapons or better are recommended. * Be aware that chopping down trees in close proximity to a Fuling village may cause Fulings to investigate. '''Forsaken powers''' are unlocked by defeating each boss and hanging their trophy on the [[Sacrificial Stones]]. By default, the player's set forsaken power is activated by [[Controls|pressing F]]. Only one forsaken power can be set at a time, which is changed out at the Sacrificial Stones.

All forsaken powers have a duration of 5 minutes. They also share the same 20-minute cooldown, which does not reset or reduce even when the player logs off, changes their active forsaken power, or sleeps.  

Activating a power locks the player into an animation for a couple of seconds. The player is unable to move or perform any action (with the exception of equipping or unequipping tools/weapons). 

When activating a forsaken power, all players within 10 meters will also receive the benefit of the forsaken power activated. Thus, a party of four players can keep a forsaken power activated virtually indefinitely by consecutively using each player's forsaken power.

*This power is best saved for when there is headwind since crosswind (perpendicular to travel direction) and tailwind are about equally good for sailing.
*This power will not affect the wind if you are too close to the [[World Edge|World's Edge]].

'''Crafting''' is the process of converting and combining [[materials]] to create new [[items]]. 

Some basic items can be crafted in the player inventory, but most items require a dedicated crafting station such as a [[Workbench]] or [[Forge]]. Most gear can also be upgraded to a higher quality, increasing its durability and other aspects.

== Crafting mechanics ==
[[File:Crafting-a-Cultivator.jpg|thumb|The crafting interface of a level 2 Forge, showing the recipe of a [[Cultivator]]. The station level is shown within the star in the top right. The craft tab allows crafting new items, whereas the upgrade tab allows upgrading gear currently in the inventory.]]

Crafting an item at a crafting station requires having the appropriate materials in the [[inventory]], as well as an available slot in the inventory for the result.

Gear that has durability can be repaired for free using the hammer icon at the side of the crafting interface at the crafting station where it was crafted (excluding the inventory). Gear that requires a higher station level to be crafed can also only be repaired at a station at that level, upgrading it does not increase this requirement.

Most weapons, tools and armors can be upgraded to higher qualities, often up to 3 times to a quality of 4. Each upgrade level requires a higher station level. Upgrading increases the durability of the item, and also improves its properties: weapons deal higher damage, while armors provide more [[Armor]]. Upgrading costs a considerable amount of resources and can double or triple the crafting cost of a given item over its cost at quality 1.

For example, the [[Troll Leather Tunic]] requires a level 2 Workbench to be crafted. Thus, it cannot be repaired at a level 1 Workbench. Upgrading it to quality 2 requires a level 3 Workbench, to quality 3 a level 4 Workbench, etc. It initially costs 6 [[Troll Hide]] to craft, but upgrading it to quality 4 costs an additional 11 Troll Hide for a total of 17.

'''Obliterators''' are buildable structures that convert any item to [[Coal]]. 

== Usage ==
Put gifts to Thor into the Obliterator and pull the lever on the right side, giving the player coal in return.

When activated, lightning strikes the lightning rod above the Obliterator dealing 400 [[Damage types|Lightning]] damage and additional 10 [[Damage types|Lightning]] damage within 2.42 meters.
== Conversion rates ==
To get 1 coal, insert:
*1 [[Trophies|Trophy]], including boss trophies, except trophies from [[Ashlands]] creatures, [[Hildir]] minibosses, [[Bear]], [[Vile]] and [[Ghost]].
*5 [[Wood]], [[Corewood]], [[Finewood]], [[Ancient Bark]], or [[Yggdrasil Wood]].
*20 [[Arrows]], except ([[Charred Arrow]])
*20 [[Bolts]], except ([[Iron Bolt]] and [[Charred Bolt]])
*10 of other items (including coal)

* The Obliterator can be placed anywhere on a flat surface and does not degrade due to rain.
* The Obliterator generates its own lightning bolt and does not require a thunderstorm to operate.
* Wood and meats can be converted to coal at a 1:1 conversion rate using a [[Charcoal Kiln]] or cooking station, making it resource-inefficient to place these in the Obliterator. 
* Currently, many trophies after Mistlands do not share the 1:1 conversion rate as other trophies, including Hildir's minibosses.

'''Ballistae''' are [[:Category:Misc structures|misc structures]] that act as an automated defense. 

A Ballista can hold 40 missiles of the same type, which will be depleted one at a time as it fires. By default, a Ballista will shoot at any [[Creatures|creature]] in an arc (±45 degrees) within a 28 meters range in front of it, including [[Player Character|player characters]] and [[Taming|tamed]] animals. Care should be taken when loading the Ballista, as it will begin shooting after the first missile is loaded if the player is standing within the firing arc.

Damage is solely based upon the [[Missiles|missile]] loaded ([[Wooden Missile]], [[Black Metal Missile]], or [[Flametal Missile]]).

==Targeting==
Targeting can be overridden by using [[trophies]]. The Ballista will usually only target and shoot enemies corresponding to the trophy used, with the exception of Draugr and Charred enemies. 
* Using trophies from [[Draugr]] or [[Draugr Elite]] will set the Ballista to target 'Draugr', including melee and ranged variants, as well as the Draugr Elite. 
* Using trophies from the [[Charred Warrior]], [[Charred Marksman]], or the [[Charred Warlock]] will set the Ballista to target 'Charred', including all of these enemies as well as the [[Charred Twitcher]]. 
* Only one trophy can be active at once, and it is not consumed, allowing for a single trophy to be used on any number of Ballistae. 
* Default targeting can be applied by using the same trophy again, or by dismantling and rebuilding the Ballista.

== Notes ==
* Considering their hostility to friendlies, such as other players and tames, in default targeting mode, caution and placement location is highly advised. Building structures which can be opened and closed, such as [[Wood Structures|wooden doors or wooden gates]], in front of the Ballista to block their field of vision ensures safe passing when needed.
* Ballistae have a slow and inaccurate aim, but quick shooting speed. Building [[Trap|traps]] to immobilize fast-moving enemies in the Ballista's range increase their effectiveness greatly. For bigger and/or slower enemies, the Ballista might need higher elevation to be effective, especially against flying creatures.
* Due to its universal target range, Ballistae can be used to train blocking skills. However, Ballistae ''cannot be parried'', so using [[Shields|tower shields]] in combination with wooden missiles due to lower damage is recommended. They can also serve as protection against other players in multiplayer servers, while still being mindful of the Ballista targeting its owner.

'''Dvergr Metal Wall''' is a buildable structure. It requires [[Copper]] to build and needs to be built within the range of a [[Black Forge]]. It can be found naturally in the world as part of some [[Dvergr (race)|Dvergr]] structures in the [[Mistlands]]. An indestructible variant can also be found inside [[Infested Mine]]s in the Mistlands.

Despite its sparse appearance, it is entirely solid; projectiles such as [[Arrows]] cannot penetrate it.

== Notes ==
* Despite the material used to build them (Copper) and having a distinct look in comparison to its iron counterpart ([[Cage Structures|Iron cage wall]]), ''they still provide the same support as iron'' regarding (vertical) [[Building stability|stability]]. This means that they can serve as a cheaper way to build higher, while also giving a very early metal a wider and important use in late stages of the game. Not mentioning the fact that it uses the easily movable Black forge (all of its materials can be [[Portal|portaled]]).
